The agency estimates that additional savings in energy are likely to accrue from fuel economy improvement measures such as reductions in vehicle weight and decreases in engine size in NPA's. These result in a decrease in steel and cast iron usage. The agency estimates a savings of steel and cast iron of 42 million pounds in MY 1975 over current levels of consumption which is 0.018 percent of the total national consumption of steel and cast iron of 236.2 billion pounds in 1975. This savings results in a savings of energy in the year of manufacture that would have been used to produce and transport the cast iron and steel, and use it in the manufacturing process, of the equivalent in BTU's of 123,000 barrels of oil which is 0.003 percent of the total national consumption of oil of 4.5 billion barrels in 1975.
